projects.title: DASH
projects.description:
For my senior design project, I am working on a website for SDSMT's Office of Institutional Research. The goal of this website is to facilitate more efficient data retrieval for office staff, as they currently have to write custom SQL scripts for multiple different databases, write Python scripts to clean and aggregate the data, and finally analyze the data and calculate statistics about it. DASH aims to eliminate the need for custom queries and cleaning scripts, and optimize calculating statistics. This will be accomplished by providing users with a website that allows them to perform queries with a GUI, upload and clean data from the current sources and seamlessly integrate it into a new database, and calculate some common statistics.

DASH is built on a Django backend and a React frontend. Most of my work thus far has been on the interface between them, such as setting up API endpoints and handling any requests that are sent their way. I have also created some components in the frontend, and handled some authentication in the backend. I also played a major role in our current database design, and worked to make it flexible and extensible, as we will be integrating new types of data as the project moves forward.

We recently hit our first major milestone by delivering on all of our MVP goals, which provided us a solid foundation to build the rest of the project on. We currently have a working prototype that lets users upload and integrate precleaned data into the database, perform queries on the data and view the results, and includes an authentication system to restrict access to the data. I'm excited to see what we can accomplish for our final project.

projects.title: Software Engineering- Tank Platform and AI Development
projects.description:
I worked as a development/DevOps team lead for the "extension" phase of the project in which we extended the functionality for a provided platform. This platform simulated a turn-based battle between "tanks", where the tanks had their own AI packages. My team managed refactoring and maintaining the legacy code, fixing bugs introduced by new features developed by other teams, and maintaining the Git repository.

For the second phase of the project, we were broken into smaller teams, and were told to write an AI package for a tank, which would then be pitted against some general tanks and then other team's tanks. In this phase, I mainly worked on developing and implementing our tank's path-finding algorithm. I also worked with the other team members on their sections, such as revamping our attack algorithm, which increased our win rate against the other teams from 30% to 50%.
